target: new: compound of two values (sinuous PATO_0001989 + nodular PATO_0002125; docs/annotation-context-patterns.md §2)
reason: Moss cell walls that are both wavy and knotty-thickened; two existing qualities stated together, not one new value.
non-erose = border not irregularly toothed: negation of PATO erose.
Pellucid means translucent, letting light through; non-pellucid is its negation.
Bryological 'sinuose' cell walls = wavy walls, PATO sinuous; non-sinuose is its negation.
Pitted cell walls are marked with pits; PATO punctate covers marking by pits, and PATO has no 'pitted'. The bearer is the cell wall.
A relation (costa not overlain by lamina cells near the apex) stated without what would cover it; not a quality of the costa alone.
Comparison stated without its second term and attribute (different in shape/size from which cells?).
A hedged comparison of submarginal cells, wrongly attached to leaf or leaf base; 'not distinctly' does not negate enlarged.
Capsule not distorted when dry = not deformed; 'when dry' goes to the specimen-condition pattern (docs/odp/06-specimen-condition.md).
Mammillose (the cell lumen bulging out) has no term and is not papillose; a term would be needed first, and two negative statements do not justify one.
Vague degree with no reference point; 'not much' does not negate enlarged.
Truncated, figurative wording about branch and shoot apices; meaningless without context.
'Not sharply' is a degree; the leaf may still be angled, so negating angular (PATO_0001977) would be wrong.
Same as non-sinuose: cell walls not wavy. The bearer is the cell or its wall.
Striolate = finely striate; 'proximally' goes to the part-of-bearer slot.
'Not strongly' is a degree, not a negation; the leaf base may still be sheathing (FLOPO:0991105).
A misspelt negation of systylious (the lid stays attached to the columella), which has no term; too rare to add one.

target: not increased thickness (PATO_0000591), bearer cell wall
reason: Thick-walled cells = cell wall of increased thickness; the negation goes on the wall as part of the cell.
A fragment of 'not tinged with brown or red'; the colours carry the meaning, the word alone is no quality.
Vesiculose (annulus of inflated cells) has no term, and swollen (PATO_0001851) is an abnormal state; a rare negation is not worth a term.
Rostrate = beaked; 'obliquely' and 'short' qualify the beak and are kept only as cue words.
'Orderly arranged' cells = placed in a repeatable, predictable pattern.

Cells bulging into papillae at the leaf tip; 'bulging' restates the papilla, and 'at tip' goes to the part slot.
'Perigonial leaves' of mosses are the perigonial bracts: a part, not a quality.

label: prosenchymatous
definition: An elongated quality inhering in a cell by virtue of the cell's being long and narrow with tapering ends that overlap those of neighbouring cells, as in prosenchyma. NOTE: Opposite of parenchymatous (short cells with blunt ends meeting end to end); used chiefly for the laminal cells of mosses.
reason: A standard botanical cell-shape term with no PATO or FLOPO equivalent; elongated alone misses the tapering, overlapping ends.
